analytic_review: Put-call parity is proved by terminal cash matching with an explicitly removed known-dividend strip. Bounds require nonnegative terminal stock and strike and positive attainable-claim prices. Strike monotonicity, vertical spread and convexity follow from payoff dominance.

Two-equation replication is unique because S R (u-d) is nonzero. Both directions of d<R<u are proved including endpoint arbitrage; u=d=R collinearity and impossible physical states are distinguished. Pricing q is inferred from traded receipts, not historical frequencies.

Backward hedge proof matches inherited wealth to the new portfolio cost. Every rebalance records stock trade plus cash change equals zero; history-dependent claims require the state history rather than accidental stock recombination.

Finite optimal stopping is proved by backward admissible-policy construction and independently verified through a bounded supermartingale argument. Writer continuation surplus is retained; selling the optimal stopped-payment replica proves the lower price bound in the complete finite market.

Nondividend call exercise theorem uses weak dominance with nonnegative rates and K>=0; ties are allowed. Negative rates reverse precisely the strike-financing inequality. The dividend counterexample includes total stock gains and only the explicitly permitted two exercise dates.

The fixed ideal-share strategy finances fees in a separate cash account. Its shortfall equals all fees accumulated from payment times. The minimum deterministic cash reserve holds only within that fixed strategy and schedule, with no optimal transaction-cost pricing claim.
No continuous-time limit, general incomplete-market unique price, empirical calibration or executable real-world hedge is silently assumed.
